item.content:encoded:
A few days ago, I decided to read some of the earliest CotBG tales and ended up rereading Like Clockwork and Reflections for the first time since, like, middle school. Both of those got me super interested in Kramer and Harken, following their storyline got me interested in the Bagman, which consequently got me interested in Game Day again.

And while I would've liked to see Kramer in the spotlight a bit more, these tales (Settling Tabs and Lost Time especially) have definitely made Harken grow on me as a character.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for being honest, I'd rather that then anything else. I'll try and address some of these issues soon.

(Edit) And now it's soon!

Fixed a couple spelling issues, as i am the worst proofreader you will ever see, ever. A lot of the other formatting things and other odd turns of phrase are just…i guess a sort of written mental tick. I have a thing for "…" as well, it seems. Sorry if it's a bit jarring, but i do try and make things more sane for the general public.

As for this:

We didn't do a lot of direct scp-related stuff
Had a report of a SCP escape

Harken's old team honestly didn't handle a lot of direct SCP stuff. They came either before or after the screaming and pain, not during. When the 106 thing happened, they had the luck of being the closest team able to respond. Just bad luck of the draw.

Harken being odd/narmy/inconsistent:

Harken really, really wants to be a bastard. He wants to be this cold, snide, aloof asshole who just moves through life. The Watchman's Comedian is probably his hero, if he would admit to such a thing. In reality, it's all a mask, at best. He puts on a show to make people either ignore him, or dislike him. However, his gooey, insecure, screwed-up center shows through sometimes. Harken isn't supposed to make you go "wow, what a cool guy!", it's more "Wow, that dude is fucked up."

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Feeling bad I had to do this to Gears of all people.

A trashed-out storefront, it bore the distinction of being across the street from a hidden Church meeting point.

I don't understand this sentence at all. Do you mean the storefront bore the distinction? Why not 'A trashed-out storefront bore the distinction..'?

slipped away with feline suppleness

This phrase also seems really off to me, for some reason. 'with feline suppleness' as a turn of phrase seems really… eh, to me… I guess

which I am varying degrees of proud and ashamed of. The CIA came knocking one day, promised all the James Bond shit.

In my head, the guy that says '…which I am varying degrees of proud and ashamed of' is not the same guy that says 'James Bond shit'. It just is odd to me.

We didn't do a lot of direct scp-related stuff
Had a report of a SCP escape

I'm rather confused as to why there's this inconsistency.

Harken's hand curled, nails pushing against his skull, holding for a few seconds, twitching, before he lowered it again, eyes returning fixedly to his shoes.

The comma spam bugs me here. Don't know if it's all good grammar and all that though, so more of a personal quibble than much else.

“I heard them dieing.”

I'm pretty sure it's dying.

Small things that kind of ruined it for me. Also Harken's ranting near the end got a bit narmy for me. I really wish I could like it,y'know, because it's you (Gears) and all. I'm sorry.
